title: Q1068976_hilbert_s_nullstellensatz
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of thousand-theorems corpus artifact Q1068976,
-- "Hilbert's Nullstellensatz": over an algebraically closed field extension,
-- the ideal vanishing on the common zero locus of a polynomial ideal in
-- finitely many variables is its radical. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module Q1068976_hilbert_s_nullstellensatz where

open import Agda.Primitive using (Level; lsuc; _⊔_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Equality using (_≡_; refl)
open import Agda.Builtin.List using (List; []; _∷_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Sigma using (Σ; _,_)

infix 4 _≠_ _↔_

data Bottom : Set where

Not :
  {a : Level} →
  Set a →
  Set a
Not A =
  A → Bottom

_≠_ :
  {a : Level} →
  {A : Set a} →
  A →
  A →
  Set a
x ≠ y =
  Not (x ≡ y)

record _↔_
  {a b : Level}
  (A : Set a)
  (B : Set b) :
  Set (a ⊔ b) where

  constructor iff
  field
    forward  : A → B
    backward : B → A

data Dec
  {a : Level}
  (A : Set a) :
  Set a where

  yes : A → Dec A
  no  : Not A → Dec A

cong :
  {a b : Level} →
  {A : Set a} →
  {B : Set b} →
  (f : A → B) →
  {x y : A} →
  x ≡ y →
  f x ≡ f y
cong f refl =
  refl

subst :
  {a b : Level} →
  {A : Set a} →
  (P : A → Set b) →
  {x y : A} →
  x ≡ y →
  P x →
  P y
subst P refl px =
  px

data Fin : Nat → Set where
  fzero : {n : Nat} → Fin (suc n)
  fsuc  : {n : Nat} → Fin n → Fin (suc n)

record Bijection
  {a b : Level}
  (A : Set a)
  (B : Set b) :
  Set (a ⊔ b) where

  field
    to      : A → B
    from    : B → A
    from-to : (x : A) → from (to x) ≡ x
    to-from : (y : B) → to (from y) ≡ y

Finite :
  {a : Level} →
  Set a →
  Set a
Finite A =
  Σ Nat (λ cardinality → Bijection A (Fin cardinality))

record CommutativeRing
  {a : Level}
  (R : Set a) :
  Set a where

  field
    zeroR oneR : R
    addR multiplyR : R → R → R
    negateR : R → R

    add-commutative :
      (x y : R) →
      addR x y ≡ addR y x
    add-associative :
      (x y z : R) →
      addR (addR x y) z ≡ addR x (addR y z)
    add-zero :
      (x : R) →
      addR x zeroR ≡ x
    add-inverse :
      (x : R) →
      addR x (negateR x) ≡ zeroR

    multiply-commutative :
      (x y : R) →
      multiplyR x y ≡ multiplyR y x
    multiply-associative :
      (x y z : R) →
      multiplyR (multiplyR x y) z ≡
      multiplyR x (multiplyR y z)
    multiply-one :
      (x : R) →
      multiplyR x oneR ≡ x
    distribute :
      (x y z : R) →
      multiplyR x (addR y z) ≡
      addR (multiplyR x y) (multiplyR x z)

record Field
  {a : Level}
  (F : Set a) :
  Set a where

  field
    ring : CommutativeRing F
    inverseF : F → F
    one-not-zero :
      CommutativeRing.oneR ring ≠
      CommutativeRing.zeroR ring
    multiply-inverse :
      (x : F) →
      x ≠ CommutativeRing.zeroR ring →
      CommutativeRing.multiplyR ring x (inverseF x) ≡
      CommutativeRing.oneR ring

record RingHom
  {a b : Level}
  {R : Set a}
  {S : Set b}
  (domain : CommutativeRing R)
  (codomain : CommutativeRing S) :
  Set (a ⊔ b) where

  field
    map : R → S
    map-zero :
      map (CommutativeRing.zeroR domain) ≡
      CommutativeRing.zeroR codomain
    map-one :
      map (CommutativeRing.oneR domain) ≡
      CommutativeRing.oneR codomain
    map-add :
      (x y : R) →
      map (CommutativeRing.addR domain x y) ≡
      CommutativeRing.addR codomain (map x) (map y)
    map-multiply :
      (x y : R) →
      map (CommutativeRing.multiplyR domain x y) ≡
      CommutativeRing.multiplyR codomain (map x) (map y)

power :
  {a : Level} →
  {R : Set a} →
  CommutativeRing R →
  R →
  Nat →
  R
power ring x zero =
  CommutativeRing.oneR ring
power ring x (suc n) =
  CommutativeRing.multiplyR ring x (power ring x n)

evaluateUnivariate :
  {a : Level} →
  {F : Set a} →
  CommutativeRing F →
  List F →
  F →
  F
evaluateUnivariate ring [] x =
  CommutativeRing.zeroR ring
evaluateUnivariate ring (coefficient ∷ coefficients) x =
  CommutativeRing.addR ring coefficient
    (CommutativeRing.multiplyR ring x
      (evaluateUnivariate ring coefficients x))

data HasNonzeroCoefficient
  {a : Level}
  {F : Set a}
  (ring : CommutativeRing F) :
  List F →
  Set a where

  here :
    {coefficient : F}
    {coefficients : List F} →
    coefficient ≠ CommutativeRing.zeroR ring →
    HasNonzeroCoefficient ring (coefficient ∷ coefficients)

  there :
    {coefficient : F}
    {coefficients : List F} →
    HasNonzeroCoefficient ring coefficients →
    HasNonzeroCoefficient ring (coefficient ∷ coefficients)

data Nonconstant
  {a : Level}
  {F : Set a}
  (ring : CommutativeRing F) :
  List F →
  Set a where

  nonconstant :
    {constant : F}
    {higher-coefficients : List F} →
    HasNonzeroCoefficient ring higher-coefficients →
    Nonconstant ring (constant ∷ higher-coefficients)

AlgebraicallyClosed :
  {a : Level} →
  {F : Set a} →
  Field F →
  Set a
AlgebraicallyClosed field-structure =
  (coefficients : List _) →
  Nonconstant (Field.ring field-structure) coefficients →
  Σ _
    (λ root →
      evaluateUnivariate
        (Field.ring field-structure)
        coefficients
        root
      ≡
      CommutativeRing.zeroR (Field.ring field-structure))

record Monomial
  {s : Level}
  (σ : Set s) :
  Set s where

  constructor monomial
  field
    exponent : σ → Nat

record Term
  {a s : Level}
  (k : Set a)
  (σ : Set s) :
  Set (a ⊔ s) where

  constructor term
  field
    coefficient : k
    monomial-part : Monomial σ

Polynomial :
  {a s : Level} →
  Set a →
  Set s →
  Set (a ⊔ s)
Polynomial k σ =
  List (Term k σ)

decideNatEquality :
  (m n : Nat) →
  Dec (m ≡ n)
decideNatEquality zero zero =
  yes refl
decideNatEquality zero (suc n) =
  no (λ ())
decideNatEquality (suc m) zero =
  no (λ ())
decideNatEquality (suc m) (suc n) with decideNatEquality m n
... | yes equality =
  yes (cong suc equality)
... | no inequality =
  no (λ { refl → inequality refl })

decideFinFunctionEquality :
  (n : Nat) →
  (f g : Fin n → Nat) →
  Dec ((i : Fin n) → f i ≡ g i)
decideFinFunctionEquality zero f g =
  yes (λ ())
decideFinFunctionEquality (suc n) f g
  with decideNatEquality (f fzero) (g fzero)
... | no unequal-at-zero =
  no (λ equality → unequal-at-zero (equality fzero))
... | yes equal-at-zero
  with decideFinFunctionEquality n
    (λ i → f (fsuc i))
    (λ i → g (fsuc i))
... | no unequal-later =
  no (λ equality → unequal-later (λ i → equality (fsuc i)))
... | yes equal-later =
  yes λ
    { fzero    → equal-at-zero
    ; (fsuc i) → equal-later i
    }

MonomialEqual :
  {s : Level} →
  {σ : Set s} →
  Monomial σ →
  Monomial σ →
  Set s
MonomialEqual left right =
  (x : _) →
  Monomial.exponent left x ≡
  Monomial.exponent right x

decideMonomialEquality :
  {s : Level} →
  {σ : Set s} →
  Finite σ →
  (left right : Monomial σ) →
  Dec (MonomialEqual left right)
decideMonomialEquality (cardinality , enumeration) left right
  with decideFinFunctionEquality cardinality
    (λ i →
      Monomial.exponent left
        (Bijection.from enumeration i))
    (λ i →
      Monomial.exponent right
        (Bijection.from enumeration i))
... | no inequality =
  no
    (λ equality →
      inequality
        (λ i →
          equality (Bijection.from enumeration i)))
... | yes equality =
  yes
    (λ x →
      subst
        (λ y →
          Monomial.exponent left y ≡
          Monomial.exponent right y)
        (Bijection.from-to enumeration x)
        (equality (Bijection.to enumeration x)))

append :
  {a : Level} →
  {A : Set a} →
  List A →
  List A →
  List A
append [] ys =
  ys
append (x ∷ xs) ys =
  x ∷ append xs ys

addMonomial :
  {s : Level} →
  {σ : Set s} →
  Monomial σ →
  Monomial σ →
  Monomial σ
addMonomial left right =
  monomial
    (λ x →
      Monomial.exponent left x +
      Monomial.exponent right x)

multiplyTerms :
  {a s : Level} →
  {k : Set a} →
  {σ : Set s} →
  CommutativeRing k →
  Term k σ →
  Term k σ →
  Term k σ
multiplyTerms ring left right =
  term
    (CommutativeRing.multiplyR ring
      (Term.coefficient left)
      (Term.coefficient right))
    (addMonomial
      (Term.monomial-part left)
      (Term.monomial-part right))

multiplyByTerm :
  {a s : Level} →
  {k : Set a} →
  {σ : Set s} →
  CommutativeRing k →
  Term k σ →
  Polynomial k σ →
  Polynomial k σ
multiplyByTerm ring left [] =
  []
multiplyByTerm ring left (right ∷ rest) =
  multiplyTerms ring left right ∷
  multiplyByTerm ring left rest

addPolynomial :
  {a s : Level} →
  {k : Set a} →
  {σ : Set s} →
  Polynomial k σ →
  Polynomial k σ →
  Polynomial k σ
addPolynomial =
  append

multiplyPolynomial :
  {a s : Level} →
  {k : Set a} →
  {σ : Set s} →
  CommutativeRing k →
  Polynomial k σ →
  Polynomial k σ →
  Polynomial k σ
multiplyPolynomial ring [] right =
  []
multiplyPolynomial ring (left ∷ rest) right =
  append
    (multiplyByTerm ring left right)
    (multiplyPolynomial ring rest right)

zeroMonomial :
  {s : Level} →
  {σ : Set s} →
  Monomial σ
zeroMonomial =
  monomial (λ _ → zero)

onePolynomial :
  {a s : Level} →
  {k : Set a} →
  {σ : Set s} →
  CommutativeRing k →
  Polynomial k σ
onePolynomial ring =
  term (CommutativeRing.oneR ring) zeroMonomial ∷ []

powerPolynomial :
  {a s : Level} →
  {k : Set a} →
  {σ : Set s} →
  CommutativeRing k →
  Polynomial k σ →
  Nat →
  Polynomial k σ
powerPolynomial ring polynomial zero =
  onePolynomial ring
powerPolynomial ring polynomial (suc n) =
  multiplyPolynomial ring polynomial
    (powerPolynomial ring polynomial n)

coefficientAt :
  {a s : Level} →
  {k : Set a} →
  {σ : Set s} →
  CommutativeRing k →
  Finite σ →
  Polynomial k σ →
  Monomial σ →
  k
coefficientAt ring finite [] target =
  CommutativeRing.zeroR ring
coefficientAt ring finite (summand ∷ rest) target
  with decideMonomialEquality finite
    (Term.monomial-part summand)
    target
... | yes equal =
  CommutativeRing.addR ring
    (Term.coefficient summand)
    (coefficientAt ring finite rest target)
... | no unequal =
  coefficientAt ring finite rest target

PolynomialEqual :
  {a s : Level} →
  {k : Set a} →
  {σ : Set s} →
  CommutativeRing k →
  Finite σ →
  Polynomial k σ →
  Polynomial k σ →
  Set (a ⊔ s)
PolynomialEqual ring finite left right =
  (monomial-part : Monomial _) →
  coefficientAt ring finite left monomial-part ≡
  coefficientAt ring finite right monomial-part

record PolynomialIdeal
  {a s : Level}
  {k : Set a}
  {σ : Set s}
  (ring : CommutativeRing k)
  (finite : Finite σ) :
  Set (lsuc (a ⊔ s)) where

  field
    member :
      Polynomial k σ →
      Set (a ⊔ s)
    membership-propositional :
      (polynomial : Polynomial k σ) →
      (u v : member polynomial) →
      u ≡ v
    respects-polynomial-equality :
      (left right : Polynomial k σ) →
      PolynomialEqual ring finite left right →
      member left →
      member right
    contains-zero :
      member []
    closed-under-addition :
      (left right : Polynomial k σ) →
      member left →
      member right →
      member (addPolynomial left right)
    absorbs-multiplication :
      (left right : Polynomial k σ) →
      member left →
      member (multiplyPolynomial ring left right)

productFin :
  {a : Level} →
  {R : Set a} →
  CommutativeRing R →
  (n : Nat) →
  (Fin n → R) →
  R
productFin ring zero values =
  CommutativeRing.oneR ring
productFin ring (suc n) values =
  CommutativeRing.multiplyR ring
    (values fzero)
    (productFin ring n (λ i → values (fsuc i)))

evaluateMonomial :
  {b s : Level} →
  {K : Set b} →
  {σ : Set s} →
  CommutativeRing K →
  Finite σ →
  (σ → K) →
  Monomial σ →
  K
evaluateMonomial ring (cardinality , enumeration) point monomial-part =
  productFin ring cardinality
    (λ i →
      power ring
        (point (Bijection.from enumeration i))
        (Monomial.exponent monomial-part
          (Bijection.from enumeration i)))

evaluateTerm :
  {a b s : Level} →
  {k : Set a} →
  {K : Set b} →
  {σ : Set s} →
  (base : CommutativeRing k) →
  (extension : CommutativeRing K) →
  RingHom base extension →
  Finite σ →
  (σ → K) →
  Term k σ →
  K
evaluateTerm base extension algebra-map finite point summand =
  CommutativeRing.multiplyR extension
    (RingHom.map algebra-map (Term.coefficient summand))
    (evaluateMonomial extension finite point
      (Term.monomial-part summand))

evaluatePolynomial :
  {a b s : Level} →
  {k : Set a} →
  {K : Set b} →
  {σ : Set s} →
  (base : CommutativeRing k) →
  (extension : CommutativeRing K) →
  RingHom base extension →
  Finite σ →
  Polynomial k σ →
  (σ → K) →
  K
evaluatePolynomial base extension algebra-map finite [] point =
  CommutativeRing.zeroR extension
evaluatePolynomial base extension algebra-map finite
  (summand ∷ rest) point =
  CommutativeRing.addR extension
    (evaluateTerm base extension algebra-map finite point summand)
    (evaluatePolynomial base extension algebra-map finite rest point)

ZeroLocus :
  {a b s : Level} →
  {k : Set a} →
  {K : Set b} →
  {σ : Set s} →
  (base : CommutativeRing k) →
  (extension : CommutativeRing K) →
  RingHom base extension →
  (finite : Finite σ) →
  PolynomialIdeal base finite →
  (σ → K) →
  Set (a ⊔ b ⊔ s)
ZeroLocus base extension algebra-map finite ideal point =
  (polynomial : Polynomial _ _) →
  PolynomialIdeal.member ideal polynomial →
  evaluatePolynomial
    base extension algebra-map finite polynomial point
  ≡
  CommutativeRing.zeroR extension

VanishesOnZeroLocus :
  {a b s : Level} →
  {k : Set a} →
  {K : Set b} →
  {σ : Set s} →
  (base : CommutativeRing k) →
  (extension : CommutativeRing K) →
  RingHom base extension →
  (finite : Finite σ) →
  PolynomialIdeal base finite →
  Polynomial k σ →
  Set (a ⊔ b ⊔ s)
VanishesOnZeroLocus base extension algebra-map finite ideal polynomial =
  (point : _ → _) →
  ZeroLocus base extension algebra-map finite ideal point →
  evaluatePolynomial
    base extension algebra-map finite polynomial point
  ≡
  CommutativeRing.zeroR extension

RadicalMember :
  {a s : Level} →
  {k : Set a} →
  {σ : Set s} →
  (ring : CommutativeRing k) →
  (finite : Finite σ) →
  PolynomialIdeal ring finite →
  Polynomial k σ →
  Set (a ⊔ s)
RadicalMember ring finite ideal polynomial =
  Σ Nat
    (λ exponent →
      PolynomialIdeal.member ideal
        (powerPolynomial ring polynomial exponent))

-- Lean: MvPolynomial.vanishingIdeal_zeroLocus_eq_radical
hilbert-s-nullstellensatz :
  (a b s : Level) →
  Set (lsuc (a ⊔ b ⊔ s))
hilbert-s-nullstellensatz a b s =
  (k : Set a) →
  (K : Set b) →
  (σ : Set s) →
  (base-field : Field k) →
  (extension-field : Field K) →
  (algebra-map :
    RingHom
      (Field.ring base-field)
      (Field.ring extension-field)) →
  AlgebraicallyClosed extension-field →
  (finite : Finite σ) →
  (ideal :
    PolynomialIdeal
      (Field.ring base-field)
      finite) →
  (polynomial : Polynomial k σ) →
  VanishesOnZeroLocus
    (Field.ring base-field)
    (Field.ring extension-field)
    algebra-map
    finite
    ideal
    polynomial
  ↔
  RadicalMember
    (Field.ring base-field)
    finite
    ideal
    polynomial

title: Q1068976_hilbert_s_nullstellensatz
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of the Thousand Theorems corpus artifact
  Q1068976, "Hilbert's Nullstellensatz": over an algebraically closed field
  extension and finitely many variables, the ideal vanishing on an ideal's
  zero locus is its radical. This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open arithmeticTheory listTheory pairTheory pred_setTheory;

val q1068976_field_def = new_definition (
  "q1068976_field_def",
  ``q1068976_field
      (z : 'a) (u : 'a)
      (add : 'a -> 'a -> 'a) (mul : 'a -> 'a -> 'a)
      (neg : 'a -> 'a) (invop : 'a -> 'a) <=>
      z <> u /\
      (!x. add z x = x) /\
      (!x. add (neg x) x = z) /\
      (!x y. add x y = add y x) /\
      (!x y z. add (add x y) z = add x (add y z)) /\
      (!x. mul u x = x) /\
      (!x y. mul x y = mul y x) /\
      (!x y z. mul (mul x y) z = mul x (mul y z)) /\
      (!x y z.
         mul x (add y z) = add (mul x y) (mul x z)) /\
      (!x. x <> z ==> mul (invop x) x = u)``);

val hilberts_nullstellensatz =
  ``!(vars : 'v set)
      (k0 : 'k) (k1 : 'k)
      (kadd : 'k -> 'k -> 'k)
      (kmul : 'k -> 'k -> 'k)
      (kneg : 'k -> 'k)
      (kinv : 'k -> 'k)
      (K0 : 'K) (K1 : 'K)
      (Kadd : 'K -> 'K -> 'K)
      (Kmul : 'K -> 'K -> 'K)
      (Kneg : 'K -> 'K)
      (Kinv : 'K -> 'K)
      (embed : 'k -> 'K).
      let is_embedding =
        (embed k0 = K0 /\
         embed k1 = K1 /\
         (!x y. embed (kadd x y) = Kadd (embed x) (embed y)) /\
         (!x y. embed (kmul x y) = Kmul (embed x) (embed y)))
      in
      let K_is_algebraically_closed =
        !coeffs : 'K list.
          1 < LENGTH coeffs /\ LAST coeffs <> K0
          ==>
          ?x : 'K.
            FOLDR (\c acc. Kadd c (Kmul x acc)) K0 coeffs = K0
      in
      let is_monomial =
        \m : 'v -> num.
          FINITE {v | m v <> 0} /\
          {v | m v <> 0} SUBSET vars
      in
      let is_polynomial =
        \p : ('v -> num) -> 'k.
          FINITE {m | p m <> k0} /\
          !m. p m <> k0 ==> is_monomial m
      in
      let polynomial_zero =
        \m : 'v -> num. k0
      in
      let polynomial_one =
        \m : 'v -> num.
          if (!v. m v = 0) then k1 else k0
      in
      let polynomial_add =
        \(p : ('v -> num) -> 'k) q m.
          kadd (p m) (q m)
      in
      let polynomial_neg =
        \(p : ('v -> num) -> 'k) m.
          kneg (p m)
      in
      let decompositions =
        \m : 'v -> num.
          {(a,b) |
             is_monomial a /\
             is_monomial b /\
             !v. a v + b v = m v}
      in
      let polynomial_mul =
        \(p : ('v -> num) -> 'k) q m.
          ITSET
            (\ab acc.
               kadd (kmul (p (FST ab)) (q (SND ab))) acc)
            (decompositions m) k0
      in
      let polynomial_pow =
        \(p : ('v -> num) -> 'k) n.
          FUNPOW (polynomial_mul p) n polynomial_one
      in
      let monomial_value =
        \(x : 'v -> 'K) (m : 'v -> num).
          ITSET
            (\v acc.
               Kmul (FUNPOW (Kmul (x v)) (m v) K1) acc)
            vars K1
      in
      let polynomial_eval =
        \(x : 'v -> 'K) (p : ('v -> num) -> 'k).
          ITSET
            (\m acc.
               Kadd (Kmul (embed (p m)) (monomial_value x m)) acc)
            {m | p m <> k0} K0
      in
      let is_ideal =
        \I : ((('v -> num) -> 'k) -> bool).
          (!p. I p ==> is_polynomial p) /\
          I polynomial_zero /\
          (!p q. I p /\ I q ==> I (polynomial_add p q)) /\
          (!p. I p ==> I (polynomial_neg p)) /\
          (!p q.
             I p /\ is_polynomial q ==> I (polynomial_mul p q))
      in
        FINITE vars /\
        q1068976_field k0 k1 kadd kmul kneg kinv /\
        q1068976_field K0 K1 Kadd Kmul Kneg Kinv /\
        is_embedding /\
        K_is_algebraically_closed
        ==>
        !I : ((('v -> num) -> 'k) -> bool).
          is_ideal I
          ==>
          !p : ('v -> num) -> 'k.
            is_polynomial p
            ==>
            ((!x : 'v -> 'K.
                (!q. I q ==> polynomial_eval x q = K0)
                ==>
                polynomial_eval x p = K0)
             <=>
             ?n : num. I (polynomial_pow p n))``;

title: Q1068976_hilbert_s_nullstellensatz
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of Thousand Theorems corpus artifact Q1068976
  (thousand-theorems__metamath__Q1068976), "Hilbert's Nullstellensatz":
  over an algebraically closed field extension, the ideal of multivariate
  polynomials vanishing on the zero locus of an arbitrary ideal equals that
  ideal's radical. This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  SetMM's S mPoly F is the multivariate polynomial ring over the field F
  with arbitrary variable carrier S. QNSAlgClosed is the usual nonconstant
  polynomial root property. QNSRadical uses positive powers in the
  multiplicative monoid of S mPoly F.

  For a field homomorphism A : F -> K, composition A o. p maps the
  coefficients of p into K. The standard SetMM evaluation map then evaluates
  that polynomial at an arbitrary assignment S -> Base(K). Thus
  QNSZeroLocus and QNSVanishingIdeal are exactly the K-valued zero locus and
  its ideal of F-coefficient polynomials. Every declaration below is an
  unproved $a statement encoding; this database contains no $p proof.
$)

$c QNSAlgClosed QNSRadical QNSZeroLocus QNSVanishingIdeal $.

qns-algebraically-closed-syntax $a wff ( QNSAlgClosed K ) $.
qns-radical-syntax $a class ( QNSRadical F S I ) $.
qns-zero-locus-syntax $a class ( QNSZeroLocus F K A S I ) $.
qns-vanishing-ideal-syntax $a class ( QNSVanishingIdeal F K A S Z ) $.

${
  $d K c p x $.

  qns-algebraically-closed-definition $a |- (
    ( QNSAlgClosed K )
    <->
    (
      K e. Field
      /\
      A. p e. ( Base ` ( 1o mPoly K ) )
        (
          A. c e. ( Base ` K )
            p =/= ( ( algSc ` ( 1o mPoly K ) ) ` c )
          ->
          E. x e. ( Base ` K )
            ( ( ( eval1 ` K ) ` p ) ` x ) = ( 0g ` K )
        )
    )
  ) $.
$}

${
  $d F I S n p $.

  qns-radical-definition $a |- (
    QNSRadical F S I
  ) = {
    p e. ( Base ` ( S mPoly F ) ) |
    E. n e. NN
      ( n ( .g ` ( mulGrp ` ( S mPoly F ) ) ) p ) e. I
  } $.
$}

${
  $d A F I K S p x $.

  qns-zero-locus-definition $a |- (
    QNSZeroLocus F K A S I
  ) = {
    x e. ( ( Base ` K ) ^m S ) |
    A. p e. I
      ( ( ( S eval K ) ` ( A o. p ) ) ` x ) = ( 0g ` K )
  } $.
$}

${
  $d A F K S Z p x $.

  qns-vanishing-ideal-definition $a |- (
    QNSVanishingIdeal F K A S Z
  ) = {
    p e. ( Base ` ( S mPoly F ) ) |
    A. x e. Z
      ( ( ( S eval K ) ` ( A o. p ) ) ` x ) = ( 0g ` K )
  } $.
$}

${
  $d A F I K S $.

  thousand-theorems-q1068976-hilbert-nullstellensatz $a |-
    A. F e. Field
      A. K e. Field
        A. A e. ( F RingHom K )
          A. S e. Fin
            A. I e. ( LIdeal ` ( S mPoly F ) )
              (
                ( QNSAlgClosed K )
                ->
                (
                  QNSVanishingIdeal F K A S
                    ( QNSZeroLocus F K A S I )
                )
                =
                ( QNSRadical F S I )
              )
  $.
$}

title: Q1068976_hilbert_s_nullstellensatz
content:
% Statement-only formalization of the thousand-theorems corpus artifact
% Q1068976 (thousand-theorems__pvs__Q1068976), "Hilbert's Nullstellensatz":
% over an algebraically closed field extension, the vanishing ideal of an
% ideal's zero locus is its radical. This file contains no proof.

hilberts_nullstellensatz_Q1068976[
  Variable: TYPE,
  k, K, Poly: TYPE+,
  zero_k, one_k: k,
  neg_k: [k -> k],
  add_k, mul_k: [k, k -> k],
  inv_k: [k -> k],
  zero_K, one_K: K,
  neg_K: [K -> K],
  add_K, mul_K: [K, K -> K],
  inv_K: [K -> K],
  algebra_map: [k -> K],
  zero_poly, one_poly: Poly,
  neg_poly: [Poly -> Poly],
  add_poly, mul_poly: [Poly, Poly -> Poly],
  coefficient: [Poly, [Variable -> nat] -> k],
  evaluate: [Poly, [Variable -> K] -> K]
]: THEORY
BEGIN

  monomial: TYPE = [Variable -> nat]
  point: TYPE = [Variable -> K]
  ideal: TYPE = [Poly -> bool]

  decomposition: TYPE =
    [# left_monomial: monomial, right_monomial: monomial #]

  zero_monomial: monomial =
    LAMBDA (v: Variable): 0

  monomial_add(left, right: monomial): monomial =
    LAMBDA (v: Variable): left(v) + right(v)

  power_K(x: K, exponent: nat): RECURSIVE K =
    IF exponent = 0 THEN
      one_K
    ELSE
      mul_K(power_K(x, exponent - 1), x)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE exponent

  power_poly(p: Poly, exponent: nat): RECURSIVE Poly =
    IF exponent = 0 THEN
      one_poly
    ELSE
      mul_poly(power_poly(p, exponent - 1), p)
    ENDIF
  MEASURE exponent

  in_variable(v: Variable, variables: list[Variable]): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES variables OF
      null: FALSE,
      cons(head, tail): v = head OR in_variable(v, tail)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE variables BY <<

  no_duplicate_variables(variables: list[Variable]): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES variables OF
      null: TRUE,
      cons(head, tail):
        NOT in_variable(head, tail)
          AND no_duplicate_variables(tail)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE variables BY <<

  exact_variable_list(variables: list[Variable]): bool =
    no_duplicate_variables(variables)
      AND (FORALL (v: Variable): in_variable(v, variables))

  in_monomial(m: monomial, monomials: list[monomial]): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES monomials OF
      null: FALSE,
      cons(head, tail): m = head OR in_monomial(m, tail)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE monomials BY <<

  no_duplicate_monomials(monomials: list[monomial]): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES monomials OF
      null: TRUE,
      cons(head, tail):
        NOT in_monomial(head, tail)
          AND no_duplicate_monomials(tail)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE monomials BY <<

  exact_support(p: Poly, monomials: list[monomial]): bool =
    no_duplicate_monomials(monomials)
      AND (FORALL (m: monomial):
        in_monomial(m, monomials)
          IFF NOT coefficient(p, m) = zero_k)

  function_exact_support(
      f: [monomial -> k],
      monomials: list[monomial]): bool =
    no_duplicate_monomials(monomials)
      AND (FORALL (m: monomial):
        in_monomial(m, monomials)
          IFF NOT f(m) = zero_k)

  finitely_supported(f: [monomial -> k]): bool =
    EXISTS (monomials: list[monomial]):
      function_exact_support(f, monomials)

  in_decomposition(
      d: decomposition,
      decompositions: list[decomposition]): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES decompositions OF
      null: FALSE,
      cons(head, tail):
        d = head OR in_decomposition(d, tail)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE decompositions BY <<

  no_duplicate_decompositions(
      decompositions: list[decomposition]): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES decompositions OF
      null: TRUE,
      cons(head, tail):
        NOT in_decomposition(head, tail)
          AND no_duplicate_decompositions(tail)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE decompositions BY <<

  exact_decompositions(
      m: monomial,
      decompositions: list[decomposition]): bool =
    no_duplicate_decompositions(decompositions)
      AND (FORALL (left, right: monomial):
        in_decomposition(
          (# left_monomial := left, right_monomial := right #),
          decompositions)
        IFF monomial_add(left, right) = m)

  convolution_sum(
      p, q: Poly,
      decompositions: list[decomposition]): RECURSIVE k =
    CASES decompositions OF
      null: zero_k,
      cons(head, tail):
        add_k(
          mul_k(
            coefficient(p, left_monomial(head)),
            coefficient(q, right_monomial(head))),
          convolution_sum(p, q, tail))
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE decompositions BY <<

  monomial_value(
      x: point,
      m: monomial,
      variables: list[Variable]): RECURSIVE K =
    CASES variables OF
      null: one_K,
      cons(head, tail):
        mul_K(
          power_K(x(head), m(head)),
          monomial_value(x, m, tail))
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE variables BY <<

  evaluation_sum(
      p: Poly,
      x: point,
      monomials: list[monomial],
      variables: list[Variable]): RECURSIVE K =
    CASES monomials OF
      null: zero_K,
      cons(head, tail):
        add_K(
          mul_K(
            algebra_map(coefficient(p, head)),
            monomial_value(x, head, variables)),
          evaluation_sum(p, x, tail, variables))
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE monomials BY <<

  list_has_nonzero(coefficients: list[K]): RECURSIVE bool =
    CASES coefficients OF
      null: FALSE,
      cons(head, tail):
        NOT head = zero_K OR list_has_nonzero(tail)
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE coefficients BY <<

  univariate_value(coefficients: list[K], x: K): RECURSIVE K =
    CASES coefficients OF
      null: zero_K,
      cons(head, tail):
        add_K(head, mul_K(x, univariate_value(tail, x)))
    ENDCASES
  MEASURE coefficients BY <<

  nonconstant_polynomial(coefficients: list[K]): bool =
    CASES coefficients OF
      null: FALSE,
      cons(constant, higher_coefficients):
        list_has_nonzero(higher_coefficients)
    ENDCASES

  field_laws_k: bool =
    NOT one_k = zero_k
      AND (FORALL (a, b: k): add_k(a, b) = add_k(b, a))
      AND (FORALL (a, b, c: k):
        add_k(add_k(a, b), c) = add_k(a, add_k(b, c)))
      AND (FORALL (a: k): add_k(a, zero_k) = a)
      AND (FORALL (a: k): add_k(a, neg_k(a)) = zero_k)
      AND (FORALL (a, b: k): mul_k(a, b) = mul_k(b, a))
      AND (FORALL (a, b, c: k):
        mul_k(mul_k(a, b), c) = mul_k(a, mul_k(b, c)))
      AND (FORALL (a: k): mul_k(a, one_k) = a)
      AND (FORALL (a, b, c: k):
        mul_k(a, add_k(b, c))
          = add_k(mul_k(a, b), mul_k(a, c)))
      AND (FORALL (a: k):
        NOT a = zero_k IMPLIES mul_k(a, inv_k(a)) = one_k)

  field_laws_K: bool =
    NOT one_K = zero_K
      AND (FORALL (a, b: K): add_K(a, b) = add_K(b, a))
      AND (FORALL (a, b, c: K):
        add_K(add_K(a, b), c) = add_K(a, add_K(b, c)))
      AND (FORALL (a: K): add_K(a, zero_K) = a)
      AND (FORALL (a: K): add_K(a, neg_K(a)) = zero_K)
      AND (FORALL (a, b: K): mul_K(a, b) = mul_K(b, a))
      AND (FORALL (a, b, c: K):
        mul_K(mul_K(a, b), c) = mul_K(a, mul_K(b, c)))
      AND (FORALL (a: K): mul_K(a, one_K) = a)
      AND (FORALL (a, b, c: K):
        mul_K(a, add_K(b, c))
          = add_K(mul_K(a, b), mul_K(a, c)))
      AND (FORALL (a: K):
        NOT a = zero_K IMPLIES mul_K(a, inv_K(a)) = one_K)

  algebra_map_laws: bool =
    algebra_map(zero_k) = zero_K
      AND algebra_map(one_k) = one_K
      AND (FORALL (a, b: k):
        algebra_map(add_k(a, b))
          = add_K(algebra_map(a), algebra_map(b)))
      AND (FORALL (a, b: k):
        algebra_map(mul_k(a, b))
          = mul_K(algebra_map(a), algebra_map(b)))

  algebraically_closed_K: bool =
    FORALL (coefficients: list[K]):
      nonconstant_polynomial(coefficients)
        IMPLIES EXISTS (x: K):
          univariate_value(coefficients, x) = zero_K

  polynomial_representation_laws: bool =
    (FORALL (p, q: Poly):
      (FORALL (m: monomial):
        coefficient(p, m) = coefficient(q, m))
      IMPLIES p = q)
      AND (FORALL (p: Poly):
        EXISTS (monomials: list[monomial]):
          exact_support(p, monomials))
      AND (FORALL (f: [monomial -> k]):
        finitely_supported(f)
          IMPLIES EXISTS (p: Poly):
            FORALL (m: monomial):
              coefficient(p, m) = f(m))
      AND (FORALL (m: monomial):
        coefficient(zero_poly, m) = zero_k)
      AND (FORALL (m: monomial):
        coefficient(one_poly, m)
          = IF m = zero_monomial THEN one_k ELSE zero_k ENDIF)
      AND (FORALL (p: Poly), (m: monomial):
        coefficient(neg_poly(p), m)
          = neg_k(coefficient(p, m)))
      AND (FORALL (p, q: Poly), (m: monomial):
        coefficient(add_poly(p, q), m)
          = add_k(coefficient(p, m), coefficient(q, m)))
      AND (FORALL (m: monomial):
        EXISTS (decompositions: list[decomposition]):
          exact_decompositions(m, decompositions))
      AND (FORALL (p, q: Poly), (m: monomial),
                  (decompositions: list[decomposition]):
        exact_decompositions(m, decompositions)
          IMPLIES coefficient(mul_poly(p, q), m)
            = convolution_sum(p, q, decompositions))
      AND (EXISTS (variables: list[Variable]):
        exact_variable_list(variables))
      AND (FORALL (p: Poly), (x: point),
                  (monomials: list[monomial]),
                  (variables: list[Variable]):
        exact_support(p, monomials)
          AND exact_variable_list(variables)
          IMPLIES evaluate(p, x)
            = evaluation_sum(p, x, monomials, variables))

  is_ideal(I: ideal): bool =
    I(zero_poly)
      AND (FORALL (p, q: Poly):
        I(p) AND I(q) IMPLIES I(add_poly(p, q)))
      AND (FORALL (p: Poly):
        I(p) IMPLIES I(neg_poly(p)))
      AND (FORALL (a, p: Poly):
        I(p) IMPLIES I(mul_poly(a, p)))

  zero_locus(I: ideal, x: point): bool =
    FORALL (p: Poly):
      I(p) IMPLIES evaluate(p, x) = zero_K

  vanishing_ideal_member(I: ideal, p: Poly): bool =
    FORALL (x: point):
      zero_locus(I, x) IMPLIES evaluate(p, x) = zero_K

  radical_member(I: ideal, p: Poly): bool =
    EXISTS (exponent: posnat):
      I(power_poly(p, exponent))

  hilberts_nullstellensatz: bool =
    (field_laws_k
      AND field_laws_K
      AND algebra_map_laws
      AND algebraically_closed_K
      AND is_finite_type[Variable]
      AND polynomial_representation_laws)
    IMPLIES
      FORALL (I: ideal):
        is_ideal(I) IMPLIES
          FORALL (p: Poly):
            vanishing_ideal_member(I, p)
              IFF radical_member(I, p)

END hilberts_nullstellensatz_Q1068976

(*

  (thousand-theorems__rocq__Q107710112), "Cantor's isomorphism theorem":
  any two countable, dense, nonempty linear orders without endpoints are
  order isomorphic. This file contains no proof.
*)

Set Universe Polymorphism.
Set Implicit Arguments.

Record q107710112_linear_order (A : Type) : Type := {
  q107710112_lt : A -> A -> Prop;
  q107710112_lt_irrefl :
    forall x : A, ~ q107710112_lt x x;
  q107710112_lt_trans :
    forall x y z : A,
      q107710112_lt x y ->
      q107710112_lt y z ->
      q107710112_lt x z;
  q107710112_lt_trichotomy :
    forall x y : A,
      q107710112_lt x y \/ x = y \/ q107710112_lt y x
}.

Arguments q107710112_lt {A} _ _ _.

Definition q107710112_countable (A : Type) : Prop :=
  exists encode : A -> nat,
    forall x y : A, encode x = encode y -> x = y.

Definition q107710112_dense
    {A : Type} (O : q107710112_linear_order A) : Prop :=
  forall x y : A,
    q107710112_lt O x y ->
    exists z : A,
      q107710112_lt O x z /\ q107710112_lt O z y.

Definition q107710112_no_minimum
    {A : Type} (O : q107710112_linear_order A) : Prop :=
  forall x : A, exists y : A, q107710112_lt O y x.

Definition q107710112_no_maximum
    {A : Type} (O : q107710112_linear_order A) : Prop :=
  forall x : A, exists y : A, q107710112_lt O x y.

Definition q107710112_nonempty (A : Type) : Prop :=
  exists x : A, True.

Definition q107710112_order_isomorphic
    {A B : Type}
    (OA : q107710112_linear_order A)
    (OB : q107710112_linear_order B) : Prop :=
  exists forward : A -> B, exists backward : B -> A,
    (forall x : A, backward (forward x) = x) /\
    (forall y : B, forward (backward y) = y) /\
    (forall x y : A,
      q107710112_lt OA x y <->
      q107710112_lt OB (forward x) (forward y)).

Theorem iso_of_countable_dense :
  forall (A B : Type)
         (OA : q107710112_linear_order A)
         (OB : q107710112_linear_order B),
    q107710112_countable A ->
    q107710112_dense OA ->
    q107710112_no_minimum OA ->
    q107710112_no_maximum OA ->
    q107710112_nonempty A ->
    q107710112_countable B ->
    q107710112_dense OB ->
    q107710112_no_minimum OB ->
    q107710112_no_maximum OB ->
    q107710112_nonempty B ->

    and no_max_b: "\<forall>x :: 'b. \<exists>y. x < y"

  "Cantor's isomorphism theorem": any two countable, dense, nonempty linear
  orders without endpoints are order isomorphic. This file contains no proof.

let Q107710112_CANTOR_ISOMORPHISM_THEOREM =
  `!ltA:A->A->bool. !ltB:B->B->bool.
     (!x:A. ~(ltA x x)) /\
     (!x y z:A. ltA x y /\ ltA y z ==> ltA x z) /\
     (!x y:A. ltA x y \/ x = y \/ ltA y x) /\
     (!x y:A. ltA x y ==> ?z:A. ltA x z /\ ltA z y) /\
     (!x:A. ?y:A. ltA y x) /\
     (!x:A. ?y:A. ltA x y) /\
     COUNTABLE (:A) /\
     (!x:B. ~(ltB x x)) /\
     (!x y z:B. ltB x y /\ ltB y z ==> ltB x z) /\
     (!x y:B. ltB x y \/ x = y \/ ltB y x) /\
     (!x y:B. ltB x y ==> ?z:B. ltB x z /\ ltB z y) /\
     (!x:B. ?y:B. ltB y x) /\
     (!x:B. ?y:B. ltB x y) /\
     COUNTABLE (:B)
     ==> ?f:A->B.
           BIJ f (:A) (:B) /\
           !x y:A. (ltB (f x) (f y) <=> ltA x y)`;;

content:
;; Statement-only formalization of Thousand Theorems corpus artifact Q107710112
;; (thousand-theorems__acl2__Q107710112), "Cantor's isomorphism theorem": any
;; two countable, dense, nonempty linear orders without endpoints are order
;; isomorphic. This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(set-inhibit-output-lst '(prove proof-tree event summary))

;; Tame APPLY$ function objects represent arbitrary carriers, strict order
;; relations, countability codes, and the maps of an order isomorphism.
;; DEFUN-SK keeps the countability and isomorphism witnesses internal.

(defun q107710112-member-p (carrier element)
  (if (apply$ carrier (list element))
      t
    nil))

(defun q107710112-less-p (less left right)
  (if (apply$ less (list left right))
      t
    nil))

(defun q107710112-unary-value (function argument)
  (apply$ function (list argument)))

;; Irreflexivity, transitivity, and trichotomy give the strict-order
;; presentation equivalent to a linear order.

(defun-sk q107710112-strict-linear-order-laws-p (carrier less)
  (forall (x y z)
    (and
     (implies
      (q107710112-member-p carrier x)
      (not (q107710112-less-p less x x)))
     (implies
      (and
       (q107710112-member-p carrier x)
       (q107710112-member-p carrier y))
      (or
       (q107710112-less-p less x y)
       (equal x y)
       (q107710112-less-p less y x)))
     (implies
      (and
       (q107710112-member-p carrier x)
       (q107710112-member-p carrier y)
       (q107710112-member-p carrier z)
       (q107710112-less-p less x y)
       (q107710112-less-p less y z))
      (q107710112-less-p less x z)))))

(defun q107710112-linear-order-p (carrier less)
  (and
   (tamep-functionp carrier)
   (tamep-functionp less)
   (q107710112-strict-linear-order-laws-p carrier less)))

;; Density and the absence of endpoints retain their existential witnesses
;; under the universal quantifiers over carrier elements.

(defun-sk q107710112-between-exists-p
    (carrier less left right)
  (exists (middle)
    (and
     (q107710112-member-p carrier middle)
     (q107710112-less-p less left middle)
     (q107710112-less-p less middle right))))

(defun-sk q107710112-densely-ordered-p (carrier less)
  (forall (left right)
    (implies
     (and
      (q107710112-member-p carrier left)
      (q107710112-member-p carrier right)
      (q107710112-less-p less left right))
     (q107710112-between-exists-p
      carrier less left right))))

(defun-sk q107710112-smaller-exists-p
    (carrier less element)
  (exists (smaller)
    (and
     (q107710112-member-p carrier smaller)
     (q107710112-less-p less smaller element))))

(defun-sk q107710112-no-min-order-p (carrier less)
  (forall (element)
    (implies
     (q107710112-member-p carrier element)
     (q107710112-smaller-exists-p
      carrier less element))))

(defun-sk q107710112-larger-exists-p
    (carrier less element)
  (exists (larger)
    (and
     (q107710112-member-p carrier larger)
     (q107710112-less-p less element larger))))

(defun-sk q107710112-no-max-order-p (carrier less)
  (forall (element)
    (implies
     (q107710112-member-p carrier element)
     (q107710112-larger-exists-p
      carrier less element))))

(defun-sk q107710112-nonempty-p (carrier)
  (exists (element)
    (q107710112-member-p carrier element)))

;; A countability code is an injective map from the carrier into the natural
;; numbers. Its existence is quantified inside Q107710112-COUNTABLE-P.

(defun-sk q107710112-countability-code-laws-p
    (carrier code)
  (forall (x y)
    (and
     (implies
      (q107710112-member-p carrier x)
      (natp (q107710112-unary-value code x)))
     (implies
      (and
       (q107710112-member-p carrier x)
       (q107710112-member-p carrier y)
       (equal
        (q107710112-unary-value code x)
        (q107710112-unary-value code y)))
      (equal x y)))))

(defun q107710112-countability-code-p (carrier code)
  (and
   (tamep-functionp code)
   (q107710112-countability-code-laws-p carrier code)))

(defun-sk q107710112-countable-p (carrier)
  (exists (code)
    (q107710112-countability-code-p carrier code)))

;; The two tame maps, their inverse equations, and strict-order equivalence
;; are exactly an order isomorphism between the two arbitrary carriers.

(defun-sk q107710112-order-isomorphism-laws-p
    (alpha alpha-less beta beta-less forward inverse)
  (forall (x y)
    (and
     (implies
      (q107710112-member-p alpha x)
      (and
       (q107710112-member-p
        beta
        (q107710112-unary-value forward x))
       (equal
        (q107710112-unary-value
         inverse
         (q107710112-unary-value forward x))
        x)))
     (implies
      (q107710112-member-p beta y)
      (and
       (q107710112-member-p
        alpha
        (q107710112-unary-value inverse y))
       (equal
        (q107710112-unary-value
         forward
         (q107710112-unary-value inverse y))
        y)))
     (implies
      (and
       (q107710112-member-p alpha x)
       (q107710112-member-p alpha y))
      (iff
       (q107710112-less-p alpha-less x y)
       (q107710112-less-p
        beta-less
        (q107710112-unary-value forward x)
        (q107710112-unary-value forward y)))))))

(defun q107710112-order-isomorphism-p
    (alpha alpha-less beta beta-less forward inverse)
  (and
   (tamep-functionp forward)
   (tamep-functionp inverse)
   (q107710112-order-isomorphism-laws-p
    alpha alpha-less beta beta-less forward inverse)))

(defun-sk q107710112-order-isomorphism-exists-p
    (alpha alpha-less beta beta-less)
  (exists (forward inverse)
    (q107710112-order-isomorphism-p
     alpha alpha-less beta beta-less forward inverse)))

(defun thousand-theorems-q107710112-cantor-isomorphism-statement
    (alpha alpha-less beta beta-less)
  (implies
   (and
    (q107710112-linear-order-p alpha alpha-less)
    (q107710112-countable-p alpha)
    (q107710112-densely-ordered-p alpha alpha-less)
    (q107710112-no-min-order-p alpha alpha-less)
    (q107710112-no-max-order-p alpha alpha-less)
    (q107710112-nonempty-p alpha)
    (q107710112-linear-order-p beta beta-less)
    (q107710112-countable-p beta)
    (q107710112-densely-ordered-p beta beta-less)
    (q107710112-no-min-order-p beta beta-less)
    (q107710112-no-max-order-p beta beta-less)
    (q107710112-nonempty-p beta))
   (q107710112-order-isomorphism-exists-p
    alpha alpha-less beta beta-less)))

title: Q107710112_cantor_s_isomorphism_theorem
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of thousand-theorems corpus artifact Q107710112,
-- "Cantor's isomorphism theorem": any two countable, dense, nonempty linear
-- orders without endpoints are order isomorphic. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module Q107710112_cantor_s_isomorphism_theorem where

open import Agda.Primitive using (Level; lsuc; _⊔_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Equality using (_≡_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat)
open import Agda.Builtin.Sigma using (Σ)

infixr 4 _×_
infixr 3 _⊎_
infix 2 _↔_

data Bottom {a : Level} : Set a where

record Top {a : Level} : Set a where
  constructor truth

Not :
  {a : Level} →
  Set a →
  Set a
Not {a} proposition =
  proposition → Bottom {a}

record _×_
  {a b : Level}
  (A : Set a)
  (B : Set b) :
  Set (a ⊔ b) where

  constructor both
  field
    first  : A
    second : B

data _⊎_
  {a b : Level}
  (A : Set a)
  (B : Set b) :
  Set (a ⊔ b) where

  left  : A → A ⊎ B
  right : B → A ⊎ B

record _↔_
  {a b : Level}
  (A : Set a)
  (B : Set b) :
  Set (a ⊔ b) where

  constructor iff
  field
    forward  : A → B
    backward : B → A

Injective :
  {a b : Level} →
  {A : Set a} →
  {B : Set b} →
  (A → B) →
  Set (a ⊔ b)
Injective {A = A} function =
  (x y : A) →
  function x ≡ function y →
  x ≡ y

Countable :
  {a : Level} →
  Set a →
  Set a
Countable A =
  Σ (A → Nat) (λ code → Injective code)

Nonempty :
  {a : Level} →
  Set a →
  Set a
Nonempty {a} A =
  Σ A (λ _ → Top {a})

record LinearOrder
  {a : Level}
  (A : Set a) :
  Set (lsuc a) where

  field
    less-than : A → A → Set a
    irreflexive :
      (x : A) →
      Not (less-than x x)
    transitive :
      (x y z : A) →
      less-than x y →
      less-than y z →
      less-than x z
    trichotomy :
      (x y : A) →
      less-than x y ⊎
      (x ≡ y ⊎ less-than y x)

Dense :
  {a : Level} →
  {A : Set a} →
  LinearOrder A →
  Set a
Dense {A = A} order =
  (x z : A) →
  LinearOrder.less-than order x z →
  Σ A
    (λ y →
      LinearOrder.less-than order x y ×
      LinearOrder.less-than order y z)

NoMinimum :
  {a : Level} →
  {A : Set a} →
  LinearOrder A →
  Set a
NoMinimum {A = A} order =
  (x : A) →
  Σ A (λ y → LinearOrder.less-than order y x)

NoMaximum :
  {a : Level} →
  {A : Set a} →
  LinearOrder A →
  Set a
NoMaximum {A = A} order =
  (x : A) →
  Σ A (λ y → LinearOrder.less-than order x y)

record OrderIsomorphism
  {a b : Level}
  {A : Set a}
  {B : Set b}
  (source : LinearOrder A)
  (target : LinearOrder B) :
  Set (a ⊔ b) where

  field
    to      : A → B
    from    : B → A
    from-to : (x : A) → from (to x) ≡ x
    to-from : (y : B) → to (from y) ≡ y
    order-equivalence :
      (x y : A) →
      LinearOrder.less-than source x y ↔
      LinearOrder.less-than target (to x) (to y)

cantor-isomorphism-theorem :
  {a b : Level} →
  Set (lsuc (a ⊔ b))
cantor-isomorphism-theorem {a} {b} =
  (A : Set a) →
  (B : Set b) →
  (orderA : LinearOrder A) →
  Countable A →
  Dense orderA →
  NoMinimum orderA →
  NoMaximum orderA →
  Nonempty A →
  (orderB : LinearOrder B) →
  Countable B →
  Dense orderB →
  NoMinimum orderB →
  NoMaximum orderB →
  Nonempty B →
  OrderIsomorphism orderA orderB

title: Q107710112_cantor_s_isomorphism_theorem
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of the Thousand Theorems corpus artifact
  Q107710112, "Cantor's isomorphism theorem": any two countable, dense,
  nonempty linear orders without endpoints are order isomorphic. This file
  contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open pred_setTheory;

val q107710112_strict_order_def = new_definition (
  "q107710112_strict_order_def",
  ``q107710112_strict_order (leq : 'a -> 'a -> bool) x y <=>
      leq x y /\ x <> y``);

val q107710112_linear_order_def = new_definition (
  "q107710112_linear_order_def",
  ``q107710112_linear_order (leq : 'a -> 'a -> bool) <=>
      (!x. leq x x) /\
      (!x y. leq x y /\ leq y x ==> x = y) /\
      (!x y z. leq x y /\ leq y z ==> leq x z) /\
      (!x y. leq x y \/ leq y x)``);

val q107710112_dense_order_def = new_definition (
  "q107710112_dense_order_def",
  ``q107710112_dense_order (leq : 'a -> 'a -> bool) <=>
      !x y.
        q107710112_strict_order leq x y
        ==>
        ?z.
          q107710112_strict_order leq x z /\
          q107710112_strict_order leq z y``);

val q107710112_no_endpoints_def = new_definition (
  "q107710112_no_endpoints_def",
  ``q107710112_no_endpoints (leq : 'a -> 'a -> bool) <=>
      (!x. ?y. q107710112_strict_order leq y x) /\
      (!x. ?y. q107710112_strict_order leq x y)``);

val iso_of_countable_dense =
  ``!(leA : 'a -> 'a -> bool) (leB : 'b -> 'b -> bool).
      q107710112_linear_order leA /\
      q107710112_dense_order leA /\
      q107710112_no_endpoints leA /\
      (?encodeA : 'a -> num.
         INJ encodeA (UNIV : 'a set) (UNIV : num set)) /\
      q107710112_linear_order leB /\
      q107710112_dense_order leB /\
      q107710112_no_endpoints leB /\
      (?encodeB : 'b -> num.
         INJ encodeB (UNIV : 'b set) (UNIV : num set))
      ==>
      ?iso : 'a -> 'b.
        BIJ iso (UNIV : 'a set) (UNIV : 'b set) /\
        !(x : 'a) (y : 'a).
          (leA x y <=> leB (iso x) (iso y))``;

title: Q107710112_cantor_s_isomorphism_theorem
content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of Thousand Theorems corpus artifact Q107710112
  (thousand-theorems__metamath__Q107710112), "Cantor's isomorphism theorem":
  any two countable, dense, nonempty linear orders without endpoints are order
  isomorphic. This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  The arbitrary Lean types are represented by set carriers a and b, with
  strict total-order relations r and s. Countability is expressed by injections
  into omega. Density and the absence of minimum and maximum elements are
  stated explicitly over each carrier.

  SetMM's predicate f Isom r , s ( a , b ) says that f is a bijection from a
  onto b and preserves and reflects the two relations. The witness f remains
  existentially quantified in the conclusion. The final declaration is the
  single unproved corpus $a statement, and this file has no $p statement.
$)

${
  $d a b f r s x y z $.

  thousand-theorems-q107710112-cantor-isomorphism $a |- (
    A. a A. b A. r A. s
      (
        (
          (
            a ~<_ _om
            /\
            b ~<_ _om
          )
          /\
          (
            (
              a =/= ( / )
              /\
              r Or a
            )
            /\
            (
              (
                A. x e. a A. y e. a
                  (
                    x r y
                    ->
                    E. z e. a
                      (
                        x r z
                        /\
                        z r y
                      )
                  )
                /\
                A. x e. a E. y e. a y r x
              )
              /\
              A. x e. a E. y e. a x r y
            )
          )
          /\
          (
            (
              b =/= ( / )
              /\
              s Or b
            )
            /\
            (
              (
                A. x e. b A. y e. b
                  (
                    x s y
                    ->
                    E. z e. b
                      (
                        x s z
                        /\
                        z s y
                      )
                  )
                /\
                A. x e. b E. y e. b y s x
              )
              /\
              A. x e. b E. y e. b x s y
            )
          )
        )
        ->
        E. f f Isom r , s ( a , b )
      )
  ) $.
$}

title: Q107710112_cantor_s_isomorphism_theorem
content:
:: Statement-only formalization of thousand-theorems corpus artifact Q107710112,
:: "Cantor's isomorphism theorem": any two countable, nonempty dense linear
:: orders without endpoints are order isomorphic. This file contains no proof.

environ
  vocabularies TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, ZFMISC_1, SUBSET_1, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1,
    FUNCT_2, ORDINAL1, CARD_1, CARD_3;
  notations TARSKI, XBOOLE_0, ZFMISC_1, SUBSET_1, ORDINAL1, CARD_1,
    RELAT_1, FUNCT_1, RELSET_1, FUNCT_2, CARD_3;
  constructors RELSET_1, FUNCT_2, CARD_3;
  registrations XBOOLE_0, SUBSET_1, ORDINAL1, RELAT_1, FUNCT_1,
    RELSET_1, FUNCT_2, CARD_1, CARD_3;
  requirements NUMERALS, SUBSET, BOOLE;

begin

::$P-
theorem
  for A,B being non empty countable set,
      r being Relation of A,A,
      s being Relation of B,B st
    (for x being Element of A holds not [x,x] in r) &
    (for x,y,z being Element of A st [x,y] in r & [y,z] in r
      holds [x,z] in r) &
    (for x,y being Element of A st x <> y
      holds [x,y] in r or [y,x] in r) &
    (for x,y being Element of A st [x,y] in r
      ex z being Element of A st [x,z] in r & [z,y] in r) &
    (for x being Element of A
      ex y being Element of A st [y,x] in r) &
    (for x being Element of A
      ex y being Element of A st [x,y] in r) &
    (for x being Element of B holds not [x,x] in s) &
    (for x,y,z being Element of B st [x,y] in s & [y,z] in s
      holds [x,z] in s) &
    (for x,y being Element of B st x <> y
      holds [x,y] in s or [y,x] in s) &
    (for x,y being Element of B st [x,y] in s
      ex z being Element of B st [x,z] in s & [z,y] in s) &
    (for x being Element of B
      ex y being Element of B st [y,x] in s) &
    (for x being Element of B
      ex y being Element of B st [x,y] in s)
  holds ex f being Function of A,B st
    f is one-to-one & rng f = B &
    for x,y being Element of A holds
      ([x,y] in r iff [f.x,f.y] in s)
proof
end;
::$P+

title: Q107710112_cantor_s_isomorphism_theorem
content:
% Statement-only formalization of the Thousand Theorems artifact Q107710112,
% "Cantor's isomorphism theorem": any two countable, dense, nonempty linear
% orders without endpoints are order isomorphic. This file contains no proof.

cantor_s_isomorphism_theorem_Q107710112[
  A: TYPE+,
  B: TYPE+,
  lt_a: [A, A -> bool],
  lt_b: [B, B -> bool]
]: THEORY
BEGIN
  strict_linear_order_a: bool =
    (FORALL (x: A): NOT lt_a(x, x))
      AND
    (FORALL (x, y, z: A):
      lt_a(x, y) AND lt_a(y, z) IMPLIES lt_a(x, z))
      AND
    (FORALL (x, y: A):
      lt_a(x, y) OR x = y OR lt_a(y, x))

  strict_linear_order_b: bool =
    (FORALL (x: B): NOT lt_b(x, x))
      AND
    (FORALL (x, y, z: B):
      lt_b(x, y) AND lt_b(y, z) IMPLIES lt_b(x, z))
      AND
    (FORALL (x, y: B):
      lt_b(x, y) OR x = y OR lt_b(y, x))

  countable_a: bool =
    EXISTS (code: [A -> nat]):
      FORALL (x, y: A):
        code(x) = code(y) IMPLIES x = y

  countable_b: bool =
    EXISTS (code: [B -> nat]):
      FORALL (x, y: B):
        code(x) = code(y) IMPLIES x = y

  densely_ordered_a: bool =
    FORALL (x, y: A):
      lt_a(x, y) IMPLIES
        EXISTS (z: A):
          lt_a(x, z) AND lt_a(z, y)

  densely_ordered_b: bool =
    FORALL (x, y: B):
      lt_b(x, y) IMPLIES
        EXISTS (z: B):
          lt_b(x, z) AND lt_b(z, y)

  no_min_order_a: bool =
    FORALL (x: A):
      EXISTS (y: A): lt_a(y, x)

  no_min_order_b: bool =
    FORALL (x: B):
      EXISTS (y: B): lt_b(y, x)

  no_max_order_a: bool =
    FORALL (x: A):
      EXISTS (y: A): lt_a(x, y)

  no_max_order_b: bool =
    FORALL (x: B):
      EXISTS (y: B): lt_b(x, y)

  nonempty_a: bool =
    EXISTS (x: A): TRUE

  nonempty_b: bool =
    EXISTS (x: B): TRUE

  injective(f: [A -> B]): bool =
    FORALL (x, y: A):
      f(x) = f(y) IMPLIES x = y

  surjective(f: [A -> B]): bool =
    FORALL (y: B):
      EXISTS (x: A): f(x) = y

  order_isomorphism(f: [A -> B]): bool =
    injective(f)
      AND surjective(f)
      AND
    (FORALL (x, y: A):
      lt_a(x, y) IFF lt_b(f(x), f(y)))

  cantor_s_isomorphism_theorem: bool =
    (strict_linear_order_a
      AND strict_linear_order_b
      AND countable_a
      AND countable_b
      AND densely_ordered_a
      AND densely_ordered_b
      AND no_min_order_a
      AND no_min_order_b
      AND no_max_order_a
      AND no_max_order_b
      AND nonempty_a
      AND nonempty_b)
    IMPLIES
      EXISTS (f: [A -> B]):
        order_isomorphism(f)
END cantor_s_isomorphism_theorem_Q107710112

-- (thousand-theorems__lean4__Q1077462), "König's theorem (set theory)":
-- if every cardinal in one indexed family is strictly smaller than its counterpart,
-- then the indexed cardinal sum is strictly smaller than the indexed cardinal product.
-- This file contains no proof.

module

public import Mathlib.SetTheory.Cardinal.Order

@[expose] public section

universe u v

namespace Q1077462

/-- König's theorem for indexed families of cardinals. -/
theorem koenig_sum_lt_prod {ι : Type u} (f g : ι → Cardinal.{v})

title: Q1077462_k_nig_s_theorem_set_theory
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of Thousand Theorems corpus artifact Q1077462
  (thousand-theorems__rocq__Q1077462), "König's theorem (set theory)":
  for arbitrary type-indexed families, pointwise strict cardinal inequalities
  imply that the dependent sum of the smaller family has strictly smaller
  cardinality than the dependent product of the larger family. This file
  contains no proof.
*)

Set Universe Polymorphism.

Definition q1077462_injective
    {A B : Type} (f : A -> B) : Prop :=
  forall x y : A, f x = f y -> x = y.

Definition q1077462_card_le (A B : Type) : Prop :=
  exists f : A -> B, q1077462_injective f.

Definition q1077462_card_lt (A B : Type) : Prop :=
  q1077462_card_le A B /\ ~ q1077462_card_le B A.

Definition q1077462_cardinal_sum
    {I : Type} (A : I -> Type) : Type :=
  { i : I & A i }.

Definition q1077462_cardinal_product
    {I : Type} (B : I -> Type) : Type :=
  forall i : I, B i.

Theorem Cardinal_sum_lt_prod :
  forall (I : Type) (A B : I -> Type),
    (forall i : I, q1077462_card_lt (A i) (B i)) ->
    q1077462_card_lt
      (q1077462_cardinal_sum A)
      (q1077462_cardinal_product B).
Admitted.

title: Q1077462_k_nig_s_theorem_set_theory
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of thousand-theorems corpus artifact Q1077462,
  "König's theorem (set theory)": for arbitrary set-indexed families of sets,
  pointwise strict inequality between fiber cardinalities implies that the
  cardinality of their disjoint sum is strictly smaller than that of their
  dependent product.
  This file contains no proof.
*)

theory Q1077462_k_nig_s_theorem_set_theory
  imports "HOL-Cardinals.Cardinal_Arithmetic"
begin

theorem konig_set_theory:
  fixes I :: "'i set"
    and F :: "'i \<Rightarrow> 'a set"
    and G :: "'i \<Rightarrow> 'b set"
  assumes pointwise: "\<And>i. i \<in> I \<Longrightarrow> |F i| <o |G i|"
  shows "|SIGMA i : I. F i| <o |PiE I G|"
  sorry

end

title: Q1077462_k_nig_s_theorem_set_theory
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of Thousand Theorems corpus artifact Q1077462,
  "König's theorem (set theory)": pointwise strict domination of cardinal
  families makes their indexed cardinal sum strictly smaller than their
  indexed cardinal product. This file contains no proof.
*)

let KONIGS_THEOREM_SET_THEORY =
  `!k:I->bool f:I->A->bool g:I->B->bool.
      (!i:I. i IN k ==> f i <_c g i)
      ==> {p:I#A | FST p IN k /\ SND p IN f (FST p)} <_c
          cartesian_product k g`;;

title: Q1077462_k_nig_s_theorem_set_theory
content:
;; Statement-only formalization of thousand-theorems corpus artifact Q1077462,
;; "König's theorem (set theory)": for arbitrary indexed families of
;; cardinals, pointwise strict inequality makes the cardinal sum of the first
;; family strictly smaller than the dependent product of the second.
;; This file contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(set-inhibit-output-lst '(prove proof-tree event summary))

;; Carriers and maps are tame APPLY$ function objects.  Existential map
;; witnesses remain inside DEFUN-SK.  Dependent functions are compared
;; pointwise, so their representation is extensional rather than syntactic.

(defun q1077462-quoted (object)
  (list 'quote object))

(defun q1077462-term-list (terms)
  (if (consp terms)
      (list
       'cons
       (car terms)
       (q1077462-term-list (cdr terms)))
    (q1077462-quoted nil)))

(defun q1077462-apply-term (function-term arguments)
  (list
   'apply$
   function-term
   (q1077462-term-list arguments)))

(defun q1077462-static-apply-term (function arguments)
  (q1077462-apply-term
   (q1077462-quoted function)
   arguments))

(defun q1077462-implies-term (hypothesis conclusion)
  (list
   'if
   hypothesis
   conclusion
   (q1077462-quoted t)))

(defun q1077462-true-function (formals)
  (list 'lambda formals (q1077462-quoted t)))

(defun q1077462-member-p (carrier object)
  (if (apply$ carrier (list object))
      t
    nil))

(defun q1077462-related-p (relation left right)
  (if (apply$ relation (list left right))
      t
    nil))

(defun q1077462-map-value (map object)
  (apply$ map (list object)))

(defun q1077462-equality-relation ()
  (list
   'lambda
   '(left right)
   (list 'equal 'left 'right)))

;; An injection between setoid carriers is a total extensional map that
;; reflects the target equivalence relation.

(defun-sk q1077462-map-total-p
    (source-carrier target-carrier map)
  (forall (object)
    (implies
     (q1077462-member-p source-carrier object)
     (q1077462-member-p
      target-carrier
      (q1077462-map-value map object)))))

(defun-sk q1077462-map-extensional-p
    (source-carrier source-equality target-equality map)
  (forall (left right)
    (implies
     (and
      (q1077462-member-p source-carrier left)
      (q1077462-member-p source-carrier right)
      (q1077462-related-p source-equality left right))
     (q1077462-related-p
      target-equality
      (q1077462-map-value map left)
      (q1077462-map-value map right)))))

(defun-sk q1077462-map-injective-p
    (source-carrier source-equality target-equality map)
  (forall (left right)
    (implies
     (and
      (q1077462-member-p source-carrier left)
      (q1077462-member-p source-carrier right)
      (q1077462-related-p
       target-equality
       (q1077462-map-value map left)
       (q1077462-map-value map right)))
     (q1077462-related-p source-equality left right))))

(defun q1077462-injection-p
    (source-carrier source-equality
     target-carrier target-equality map)
  (and
   (tamep-functionp source-carrier)
   (tamep-functionp source-equality)
   (tamep-functionp target-carrier)
   (tamep-functionp target-equality)
   (tamep-functionp map)
   (q1077462-map-total-p
    source-carrier target-carrier map)
   (q1077462-map-extensional-p
    source-carrier source-equality target-equality map)
   (q1077462-map-injective-p
    source-carrier source-equality target-equality map)))

(defun-sk q1077462-injection-exists-p
    (source-carrier source-equality
     target-carrier target-equality)
  (exists (map)
    (q1077462-injection-p
     source-carrier source-equality
     target-carrier target-equality map)))

;; Strict cardinal inequality is injection in the forward direction and no
;; injection in the reverse direction.

(defun q1077462-cardinal-lt-p
    (left-carrier left-equality
     right-carrier right-equality)
  (and
   (q1077462-injection-exists-p
    left-carrier left-equality
    right-carrier right-equality)
   (not
    (q1077462-injection-exists-p
     right-carrier right-equality
     left-carrier left-equality))))

(defun q1077462-fiber-carrier (family index)
  (apply$ family (list index)))

(defun-sk q1077462-family-valid-p (index-carrier family)
  (forall (index)
    (implies
     (q1077462-member-p index-carrier index)
     (tamep-functionp
      (q1077462-fiber-carrier family index)))))

(defun-sk q1077462-pointwise-lt-p
    (index-carrier left-family right-family)
  (forall (index)
    (implies
     (q1077462-member-p index-carrier index)
     (q1077462-cardinal-lt-p
      (q1077462-fiber-carrier left-family index)
      (q1077462-equality-relation)
      (q1077462-fiber-carrier right-family index)
      (q1077462-equality-relation)))))

;; The indexed cardinal sum is represented by dependent pairs (index, value).

(defun q1077462-sum-member-p
    (index-carrier family pair)
  (and
   (true-listp pair)
   (equal (len pair) 2)
   (q1077462-member-p index-carrier (nth 0 pair))
   (q1077462-member-p
    (q1077462-fiber-carrier family (nth 0 pair))
    (nth 1 pair))))

(defun q1077462-sum-carrier
    (index-carrier family)

   'lambda

-- Statement-only formalization of thousand-theorems corpus artifact Q1077462,
-- "König's theorem (set theory)": pointwise strict cardinal inequalities between
-- arbitrary type families imply that their dependent sum has strictly smaller
-- cardinality than their dependent product. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module Q1077462_k_nig_s_theorem_set_theory where

open import Agda.Primitive using (Level; lsuc; _⊔_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Equality using (_≡_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Sigma using (Σ)

data Bottom : Set where

Not :
  {a : Level} ->
  Set a ->
  Set a
Not proposition =
  proposition -> Bottom

Injective :
  {a b : Level} ->
  {A : Set a} ->
  {B : Set b} ->
  (A -> B) ->
  Set (a ⊔ b)
Injective {A = A} function =
  (x y : A) ->
  function x ≡ function y ->
  x ≡ y

record Injection
  {a b : Level}
  (A : Set a)
  (B : Set b) :
  Set (a ⊔ b) where

  field
    map       : A -> B
    injective : Injective map

record StrictlySmaller
  {a b : Level}
  (A : Set a)
  (B : Set b) :
  Set (a ⊔ b) where

  field
    embeds       : Injection A B
    no-embedding : Not (Injection B A)

koenigs-theorem :
  {i c : Level} ->
  Set (lsuc (i ⊔ c))
koenigs-theorem {i} {c} =
  (I : Set i) ->
  (A : I -> Set c) ->
  (B : I -> Set c) ->
  ((index : I) -> StrictlySmaller (A index) (B index)) ->
  StrictlySmaller
    (Σ I A)
    ((index : I) -> B index)

  (thousand-theorems__metamath__Q1077462), "König's theorem (set theory)":
  for arbitrary cardinal-valued families over an arbitrary index set,
  pointwise strict inequality makes the cardinal sum strictly smaller than
  the cardinal product. This file contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  m and n are total families on a. Requiring each value to be fixed by card
  says exactly that the families are cardinal-valued. The tagged union
  U_ i e. a ( { i } X. ( m ` i ) ) is the dependent disjoint union whose
  cardinality is the source Cardinal.sum, while X_ i e. a ( n ` i ) is the
  dependent function space whose cardinality is Cardinal.prod. SetMM's ~<
  is strict cardinal domination.

  The final declaration is the single unproved $a corpus statement. This root
  artifact contains no $p declaration; the included lib/set.mm database
  supplies the standard SetMM language and proved library.
$)

${
  $d a i $.  $d i m $.  $d i n $.

  thousand-theorems-q1077462-konig $a |- (
    A. a A. m A. n
      (
        (
          (
            m Fn a
            /\
            n Fn a
          )
          /\
          A. i e. a
            (
              (
                ( card ` ( m ` i ) ) = ( m ` i )
                /\
                ( card ` ( n ` i ) ) = ( n ` i )
              )
              /\
              ( m ` i ) ~< ( n ` i )
            )
        )
        ->
        (
          U_ i e. a ( { i } X. ( m ` i ) )
          ~<
          X_ i e. a ( n ` i )
        )
      )
  ) $.
$}

title: Q1077462_k_nig_s_theorem_set_theory
content:
% Statement-only formalization of the Thousand Theorems artifact Q1077462,
% "König's theorem (set theory)": a pointwise strict inequality between
% cardinal families implies that their indexed sum is strictly smaller than
% their indexed product. This file contains no proof.

koenig_set_theory_Q1077462[
  I: TYPE,
  U: TYPE+,
  F, G: [I -> [U -> bool]]
]: THEORY
BEGIN
  point_set: TYPE = [U -> bool]
  point_relation: TYPE = [U, U -> bool]
  sum_product_relation: TYPE = [I, U, [I -> U] -> bool]
  product_sum_relation: TYPE = [[I -> U], I, U -> bool]

  injects(A, B: point_set, relation: point_relation): bool =
    (FORALL (x, y: U):
      relation(x, y) IMPLIES A(x) AND B(y))
    AND
    (FORALL (x: U):
      A(x) IMPLIES EXISTS (y: U): relation(x, y))
    AND
    (FORALL (x, y, z: U):
      (relation(x, y) AND relation(x, z)) IMPLIES y = z)
    AND
    (FORALL (x, y, z: U):
      (relation(x, z) AND relation(y, z)) IMPLIES x = y)

  strictly_smaller(A, B: point_set): bool =
    (EXISTS (relation: point_relation): injects(A, B, relation))
    AND
    NOT (EXISTS (relation: point_relation): injects(B, A, relation))

  pointwise_strict: bool =
    FORALL (i: I): strictly_smaller(F(i), G(i))

  product_member(choice: [I -> U]): bool =
    FORALL (i: I): G(i)(choice(i))

  sum_injects_product(relation: sum_product_relation): bool =
    (FORALL (i: I), (x: U), (choice: [I -> U]):
      relation(i, x, choice)
        IMPLIES F(i)(x) AND product_member(choice))
    AND
    (FORALL (i: I), (x: U):
      F(i)(x)
        IMPLIES
          EXISTS (choice: [I -> U]): relation(i, x, choice))
    AND
    (FORALL (i: I), (x: U), (left, right: [I -> U]):
      (relation(i, x, left) AND relation(i, x, right))
        IMPLIES left = right)
    AND
    (FORALL (i, j: I), (x, y: U), (choice: [I -> U]):
      (relation(i, x, choice) AND relation(j, y, choice))
        IMPLIES i = j AND x = y)

  product_injects_sum(relation: product_sum_relation): bool =
    (FORALL (choice: [I -> U]), (i: I), (x: U):
      relation(choice, i, x)
        IMPLIES product_member(choice) AND F(i)(x))
    AND
    (FORALL (choice: [I -> U]):
      product_member(choice)
        IMPLIES
          EXISTS (i: I), (x: U): relation(choice, i, x))
    AND
    (FORALL (choice: [I -> U]), (i, j: I), (x, y: U):
      (relation(choice, i, x) AND relation(choice, j, y))
        IMPLIES i = j AND x = y)
    AND
    (FORALL (left, right: [I -> U]), (i: I), (x: U):
      (relation(left, i, x) AND relation(right, i, x))
        IMPLIES left = right)

  koenig_theorem: bool =
    pointwise_strict
      IMPLIES
        (EXISTS (relation: sum_product_relation):
          sum_injects_product(relation))
        AND
        NOT (EXISTS (relation: product_sum_relation):
          product_injects_sum(relation))
END koenig_set_theory_Q1077462

title: Q1082910_euler_s_partition_theorem
content:
(*
  Statement-only formalization of Thousand Theorems corpus artifact Q1082910
  (thousand-theorems__rocq__Q1082910), "Euler's partition theorem": for every
  natural number, the number of partitions into odd positive parts equals the
  number of partitions into distinct positive parts. This file contains no
  proof.
*)

From Stdlib Require Import List Sorting.

Import ListNotations.

Fixpoint q1082910_sum_parts (parts : list nat) : nat :=
  match parts with
  | [] => 0
  | x :: xs => x + q1082910_sum_parts xs
  end.

(* A nondecreasing list of positive parts canonically represents an unordered
   partition; the empty list is the unique partition of zero. *)
Definition q1082910_partition (n : nat) (parts : list nat) : Prop :=
  Forall (fun x => 0 < x) parts /\
  StronglySorted le parts /\
  q1082910_sum_parts parts = n.

Definition q1082910_distinct_partition
    (n : nat) (parts : list nat) : Prop :=
  q1082910_partition n parts /\ NoDup parts.

Definition q1082910_odd_part (x : nat) : Prop :=
  exists k : nat, x = 2 * k + 1.

Definition q1082910_odd_partition
    (n : nat) (parts : list nat) : Prop :=
  q1082910_partition n parts /\
  Forall q1082910_odd_part parts.

Definition q1082910_has_cardinality
    (P : list nat -> Prop) (card : nat) : Prop :=
  exists enumeration : list (list nat),
    NoDup enumeration /\
    length enumeration = card /\
    forall parts : list nat,
      In parts enumeration <-> P parts.

Theorem q1082910_euler_partition_theorem :
  forall n : nat,
    exists card : nat,
      q1082910_has_cardinality
        (q1082910_odd_partition n) card /\
      q1082910_has_cardinality
        (q1082910_distinct_partition n) card.
Admitted.

;; thousand-theorems__acl2__Q1082910, "Euler's partition theorem": for every
;; natural number n, the number of partitions of n into odd positive parts
;; equals the number of partitions of n into distinct positive parts. The
;; recursive counters enumerate these two finite partition classes. This file
;; contains no proof.

(in-package "ACL2")

(defun q1082910-count-distinct-partitions-through-part
    (remaining part)
  (declare (xargs :measure (nfix part)))
  (if (and (natp remaining)
           (natp part))
      (if (zp part)
          (if (zp remaining) 1 0)
        (+ (q1082910-count-distinct-partitions-through-part
            remaining (- part 1))
           (if (<= part remaining)
               (q1082910-count-distinct-partitions-through-part
                (- remaining part) (- part 1))

(defun q1082910-count-odd-partitions-through-part
    (remaining part)

  (if (and (natp remaining)
           (natp part))

        (if (equal (mod part 2) 0)

title: Q1082910_euler_s_partition_theorem
content:
-- Statement-only formalization of thousand-theorems corpus artifact Q1082910,
-- "Euler's partition theorem": for every natural number, the finite numbers
-- of partitions into odd positive parts and into distinct positive parts are
-- equal. This file contains no proof.

{-# OPTIONS --safe #-}

module Q1082910_euler_s_partition_theorem where

open import Agda.Builtin.Bool using (Bool; false; true)
open import Agda.Builtin.Equality using (_≡_)
open import Agda.Builtin.List using (List; []; _∷_)
open import Agda.Builtin.Nat using (Nat; zero; suc; _+_)

infixr 5 _++_
infixr 6 _and_

_++_ :
  {A : Set} →
  List A →
  List A →
  List A
[] ++ ys = ys
(x ∷ xs) ++ ys = x ∷ (xs ++ ys)

map :
  {A B : Set} →
  (A → B) →
  List A →
  List B
map f [] = []
map f (x ∷ xs) = f x ∷ map f xs

concat :
  {A : Set} →
  List (List A) →
  List A
concat [] = []
concat (xs ∷ xss) = xs ++ concat xss

concatMap :
  {A B : Set} →
  (A → List B) →
  List A →
  List B
concatMap f xs = concat (map f xs)

_and_ :
  Bool →
  Bool →
  Bool
true and right = right
false and right = false

equalNat :
  Nat →
  Nat →
  Bool
equalNat zero zero = true
equalNat zero (suc right) = false
equalNat (suc left) zero = false
equalNat (suc left) (suc right) = equalNat left right

lessEqual :
  Nat →
  Nat →
  Bool
lessEqual zero right = true
lessEqual (suc left) zero = false
lessEqual (suc left) (suc right) = lessEqual left right

lessThan :
  Nat →
  Nat →
  Bool
lessThan left right = lessEqual (suc left) right

positive :
  Nat →
  Bool
positive zero = false
positive (suc n) = true

odd :
  Nat →
  Bool
odd zero = false
odd (suc zero) = true
odd (suc (suc n)) = odd n

all :
  (Nat → Bool) →
  List Nat →
  Bool
all predicate [] = true
all predicate (x ∷ xs) =
  predicate x and all predicate xs

sum :
  List Nat →
  Nat
sum [] = zero
sum (x ∷ xs) = x + sum xs

nonIncreasing :
  List Nat →
  Bool
nonIncreasing [] = true
nonIncreasing (x ∷ []) = true
nonIncreasing (x ∷ y ∷ xs) =
  lessEqual y x and nonIncreasing (y ∷ xs)

strictlyDecreasing :
  List Nat →
  Bool
strictlyDecreasing [] = true
strictlyDecreasing (x ∷ []) = true
strictlyDecreasing (x ∷ y ∷ xs) =
  lessThan y x and strictlyDecreasing (y ∷ xs)

positivePartsUpTo :
  Nat →
  List Nat
positivePartsUpTo zero = []
positivePartsUpTo (suc n) =
  suc n ∷ positivePartsUpTo n

listsOfLength :
  Nat →
  List Nat →
  List (List Nat)
listsOfLength zero alphabet = [] ∷ []
listsOfLength (suc length) alphabet =
  concatMap
    (λ head →
      map
        (λ tail → head ∷ tail)
        (listsOfLength length alphabet))
    alphabet

listsUpToLength :
  Nat →
  List Nat →
  List (List Nat)
listsUpToLength zero alphabet = [] ∷ []
listsUpToLength (suc bound) alphabet =
  listsUpToLength bound alphabet ++
  listsOfLength (suc bound) alphabet

partitionCandidates :
  Nat →
  List (List Nat)
partitionCandidates n =
  listsUpToLength n (positivePartsUpTo n)

isOddPartition :
  Nat →
  List Nat →
  Bool
isOddPartition n parts =
  equalNat (sum parts) n and
  (all positive parts and
   (nonIncreasing parts and all odd parts))

isDistinctPartition :
  Nat →
  List Nat →
  Bool
isDistinctPartition n parts =
  equalNat (sum parts) n and
  (all positive parts and strictlyDecreasing parts)

countSatisfying :
  (List Nat → Bool) →
  List (List Nat) →
  Nat
countSatisfying predicate [] = zero
countSatisfying predicate (parts ∷ rest)
  with predicate parts
... | true = suc (countSatisfying predicate rest)
... | false = countSatisfying predicate rest

oddPartitionCount :
  Nat →
  Nat
oddPartitionCount n =
  countSatisfying
    (isOddPartition n)
    (partitionCandidates n)

distinctPartitionCount :
  Nat →
  Nat
distinctPartitionCount n =
  countSatisfying
    (isDistinctPartition n)
    (partitionCandidates n)

euler-partition-theorem : Set
euler-partition-theorem =
  (n : Nat) →
  oddPartitionCount n ≡ distinctPartitionCount n

  for each natural number n, the finite sets of partitions of n into odd
  positive parts and into distinct positive parts have equal cardinality.
  This file contains no proof.
*)

open HolKernel Parse boolLib;
open arithmeticTheory pred_setTheory;

val card_odds_eq_card_distincts =
  ``!n : num.
      let is_partition =
        \p : num -> num.
          (!i. p i <> 0 ==> 1 <= i /\ i <= n) /\
          SIGMA (\i. p i * i) (count (SUC n)) = n
      in
        let distinct_partitions =
          {p : num -> num |
             is_partition p /\ (!i. p i <= 1)}
        in
        let odd_partitions =
          {p : num -> num |
             is_partition p /\ (!i. p i <> 0 ==> ODD i)}
        in
          FINITE distinct_partitions /\
          FINITE odd_partitions /\
          CARD odd_partitions = CARD distinct_partitions``;

content:
$(
  Statement-only formalization of Thousand Theorems corpus artifact Q1082910
  (thousand-theorems__metamath__Q1082910), "Euler's partition theorem": for
  every natural number, the number of partitions into odd positive parts
  equals the number of partitions into distinct positive parts. This file
  contains no proof.
$)

$[ lib/set.mm $]

$(
  A partition of m is represented by a finitely supported multiplicity
  function f : NN --> NN0 whose weighted sum is m. Its support is
  ( `' f " NN ), the positive part sizes having nonzero multiplicity.

  The left restricted set requires every supported part size to be odd,
  expressed as not divisible by two. The right restricted set requires every
  multiplicity to be at most one. Thus the two finite cardinalities encode
  Nat.Partition.odds N and Nat.Partition.distincts N, respectively.

  The declaration below is the single unproved $a corpus statement; it
  introduces no $p proof statement.
$)

${
  $d f g k m n $.

  thousand-theorems-q1082910-euler-partition $a
    |- A. m e. NN0
         (
           ( # `
             { g e.
               { f e. ( NN0 ^m NN ) |
                 ( ( `' f " NN ) e. Fin /\
                   ( sum_ k e. NN ( ( f ` k ) x. k ) ) = m
                 )
               } |
               A. n e. ( `' g " NN ) -. 2 || n
             }
           )
           =
           ( # `
             { g e.
               { f e. ( NN0 ^m NN ) |
                 ( ( `' f " NN ) e. Fin /\
                   ( sum_ k e. NN ( ( f ` k ) x. k ) ) = m
                 )
               } |
               A. n e. NN ( g ` n ) <_ 1
             }
           )
         )
  $.
$}
